sentences.text: Bhaiyalal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 August, 2024

Author: Anuradha Shukla
Bench: Anuradha Shukla

1 Mc
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Anuradha Shukla

On The 12th Of August, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 22828 of 2024
 Bhaiyalal
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Santosh Kumar Singh - Advocate for the applicant.
 Ms. Samta Jain - Government Advocate for the State.
 Order

This is second application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.664/2023 dated 15.06.2023 registered at Police Station Sarai, District Singrauli, for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 120B, 498A, 34 of IPC.

His earlier bail application (M.Cr.C. No.55548/2023)
was dismissed on merits vide order dated 10.01.2024 by this Court.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in judicial custody since 16.06.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant is the permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned respective counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

This repeat bail application has been argued on the ground of delay in trial and hostile testimony of relatives of deceased and for this certified copy of statements of Manilal@ Mannilal Rawat and Lallu Rawat have been relied upon.
The applicant is facing trial for the offence under Section 302, 498A etc. of IPC for the murder of his wife and pretending the death to be accidental.
In such a serious nature of offence, the custody period of applicant since 16.06.2023 cannot be adjudged to be considerable.

Further, the relatives of Bhaiyalal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96663068/
1 deceased have supported the prosecution case on considerable material points.

sentences.text: At this stage, the finer appreciation of evidence is not possible.
Having considered these facts and also the fact that earlier bail application was dismissed on merits under M.Cr.C. No.55548/2023, this repeat bail application is also dismissed.
